title: Your Body Is Not The One You Were Born With
description:
Most of your cells are replaced on a schedule you'd never guess — except for a few parts that are with you for life. Here's the real timeline.

#shorts #sciencefacts #biology

scenes.text: Almost none of the atoms in your body were there ten years ago. Most of you gets rebuilt on a schedule.
Skin replaces itself roughly every month. Red blood cells last about four months before your body makes new ones.
Your entire skeleton is rebuilt cell by cell over about a decade, even though bone feels permanent.
But a few parts never get replaced. The lens of your eye and the enamel on your teeth form before birth and stay with you for life.
Most of the neurons in your brain's cortex are also original equipment, wired in during early development and never swapped out.
So you're not one body. You're a slow, ongoing renovation with a few rooms that never got touched.
